one_pager.big_idea: To find out whether something really works, scientists run fair trials with a control group, a placebo and blinding, and they treat the people in their trials honestly and with respect.
goals: I can explain why a fair trial needs a control group, a placebo, blinding and a big enough sample.
I can compare two groups' results using means and ranges and give an honest verdict, and discuss what makes research with people ethical.

flow.what: Give out the checkpoint, read the instructions, keep time; students work alone and in silence with their own pens; collect at exactly 10 minutes and put the papers away. The incoming teacher observes. Slides 1 to 2.

Tu Youyou story: an idea from a text more than 1,600 years old, tested carefully, leading to artemisinin and a Nobel Prize. 'Should we believe an idea because it is old? How would you find out?' Slides 3 to 4.

Follow the lucky pen script exactly: a pen and a folded card for each student (alternating versions), code written on the recall sheet; study the word list for 60 seconds; count backwards in threes for 30 seconds; recall for 2 minutes with the new pen (English or Chinese); swap and mark out of 20. Slides 5 to 8.

Keep the promise straight away: reveal both cards and that every pen is identical; apologise for the trick. Teach control group, placebo, placebo effect, blind test, double-blind, random allocation and sample size. Slides 9 to 10.

Recorders call out group scores by code, never by name; class means and ranges calculated together on the board; group results table; worksheet Core and Stretch. Usual verdict: not enough evidence yet. Slide 11.

Ethics debrief with the card in pairs, any language, share with a frame, and the chance to withdraw a score with a cross on the recall sheet (5 min); exit ticket (2 min); logbook line (2 min). Use the last 2 minutes to introduce the incoming teacher. Slides 12 to 13.

one_pager.practical: Lucky pen memory trial: every student gets an identical pen and a folded card (Code 41 says it is a special 'Focus Pen', Code 52 is the control), studies 20 words for 60 seconds, counts backwards for 30 seconds, recalls for 2 minutes and a partner marks the sheet out of 20. The class then compares the two groups' means and ranges and gives a verdict on the claim 'Believing your pen is lucky improves your memory.'
one_pager.assessment: Checkpoint out of 12 (6 questions, based on skills check question types 1 to 6), entered in the tracker (column 'W5 checkpoint') before the handover note is written. Output: trial results (group results table and worksheet Stretch). Exit ticket: placebo, control group and blind test. Logbook line: 'A fair trial needs ___ because ___.'
hazards: No practical hazards beyond normal classroom rules.
Mild deception in the memory test (about 7 minutes): explain the secret in the same lesson, straight after the test.
Taking part is voluntary: a student may watch instead; any student may withdraw their score after the debrief.
Scores are anonymous (codes only, never names); never use scores to compare individual students.
one_pager.language_note: Frames: 'The control group was ___ because ___.' 'The data suggests ___; however, ___.' 'To be more confident, we would need ___.' 'I think it was / was not OK because ___.' Chinese talk is welcome in the ethics debrief; report back in English with a frame. Recall may be written in English or Chinese; both count and spelling does not matter (the same rule for both groups). Checkpoint: read any question aloud in English if asked, explain everyday words, not science words; accept Chinese for Question 4. Traps: 'blind' here does not mean unable to see; 'trial' also means a court case; a placebo is a fake medicine, and the idea also applies to fake 'lucky' objects.
watch_out: Do not give the secret away before the reveal: brief the incoming teacher, treat both groups in exactly the same way and do not look at codes while students are working.
Never cut the reveal or the chance to withdraw scores. If time is short: recall 90 seconds, skip the Part B calculations and give the class means from the board, cut Challenge.

'If the lucky group scored higher, the pen works': the pens were identical, so any real difference comes from belief (placebo effect) or chance; compare a small difference in means with the ranges and the sample size.
'The placebo effect means the person is stupid or fooled': expectations affect everyone, including scientists.
one_pager.next_week_link: The current teacher marks the checkpoints, enters the scores and completes one handover note per class; the 30-minute walkthrough is booked before the first Week 6 lesson. Week 6: the incoming teacher leads and starts the project phase with the Mpemba mystery (does hot water really freeze faster than cold?), Plan A or Plan B depending on the freezer decision. The Week 6 Do Now asks which group was the control group in the lucky pen trial (Code 52). The checkpoint answers may be gone through in Week 6. In Week 7, human-participant claims (7, 8 and 12) need the same ethics: voluntary, anonymous, no pressure. During this week, for Week 6 Plan A: 2 to 3 kg ice on the day, salt, cups, 12 to 24 small tubes, thermometers, stopwatches, gloves, goggles, teacher warm water; Plan B: 6 to 12 thermometers, water at about 60 °C and 35 °C.

open_questions: Checkpoint paper: assessment/Checkpoint_Y9.md asks for 'one side of A4', but the design (Checkpoint.dc.html and Checkpoint-2.dc.html) has 2 pages, entered as 1 sheet double-sided. Confirm double-sided printing.

Pen cards: Y9_W05_Fair_trials.md section 6b says 8 cards per A4 sheet and also 'print as A6 and fold' to A7; only 4 A6 cards fit on A4. The design (Pen-cards-inside.dc.html) has 8 smaller cards per sheet. Is the smaller card acceptable, and should the cards be on paper or card (not stated)?
Pen cards and reuse: the kit card says collect the cards but, unlike the word lists, does not say they are reused. Entered as 3 new sheets per class; could one deck serve every class?

Worksheet (Main.dc.html, Worksheet-2.dc.html): the exit ticket strip at the foot of page 2 is on the back of the Stretch writing lines on page 1, so cutting it off removes part of page 1; and Core 2 on page 1 says 'Use the word bank' while the fold-under word bank is on page 2. Collect the whole worksheet instead, or print single-sided (2 sheets per copy)?

Withdrawn scores: the kit card says 'remove any with a cross before entering results', but in the lesson plan the class results are collected and the means calculated in Do Part B, before students are offered the chance to withdraw in Think and Reflect. Should the class means be recalculated after the lesson, and where are the results entered?
Think and Reflect is 9 minutes (ethics 5, exit tickets 2, logbook 2), but the lesson plan also says 'Use the last 2 minutes to introduce' the incoming teacher. Which part gives way?
Checkpoint timing: assessment/Checkpoint_Y9.md and the Teacher Guide give 10 minutes working plus 1 minute to give out and collect; the lesson plan allows 10 minutes in total.

Handover note: section 7 of Y9_W05_Fair_trials.md (notes for the incoming teacher) says 'Complete the handover note after this lesson', but the Teacher Guide says the current teacher completes it. Entered as a task for the current teacher.

Answer key, Stretch 1 model (Y9_W05_Fair_trials.md): the means are given as 10.2 and 9.8 but 'the difference was about 0.3 words'; the rounded means differ by 0.4 (unrounded, 10.17 minus 9.83 is 0.33).

No spares are stated for the checkpoint papers, worksheets, recall sheets or pens (24 each). Add spares? The files also do not say how to deal the pen cards if fewer than 24 students are present, or whether an absent student sits the checkpoint later.

A5 items (word list, recall sheet, group results table, ethics debrief card, kit card): the files do not say whether they are printed on A5 or 2 up on A4 and cut; cutting the pen cards also needs scissors or a guillotine, which are not listed.
The 24 identical pens are 'buy or collect' on the kit card and on the Teacher Guide's kit order before Week 1; the Year 9 requisition was not checked. Confirm they are ordered.

Where do the group results tables and marked worksheets go after the lesson (logbook, class box or assessment folder)? The files only say to collect exit tickets and recall sheets and to store checkpoint papers.
